globalRequirements: Create a dedicated Kubernetes navigation/workspace group with Human access, Token validation, Authorization/RBAC, Workload identity, and Delegation/extensions families. JWT foundations are their own shared family linked from K8s and existing OAuth/OIDC/JWE lessons. Do not bury Kubernetes inside generic OAuth or silently duplicate existing lessons.

Use canonical events, explicit actor-local holdings and immutable artifact/generation IDs. Track received bytes, parsed untrusted claims, verified signature, validated claims, mapped userInfo, authorization input/verdict, admission proposal/verdict, persisted object and response separately. Reading a claim never creates permission.

Model API authentication/RBAC/admission as local API-server stages; different swimlanes may explain responsibilities but must not fabricate network hops. The API server may read from watch caches; a symbolic storage boundary must not imply every read makes a new etcd network RPC.

Each scenario has a fixed happy path and independently selectable failures with declared policy. Branches must alter the relevant request/claim/key/rule/state, not only the narration. Do not silently recover into another authenticator or grant.

JWT validation requires primary-source rules and profile-specific requirements. Public key retrieval is not proof of trust by itself. Never expose issuer private keys, refresh tokens or plaintext JWE contents to actors that do not possess them. Bearer token display is synthetic and clearly labeled.

Maintain overview/field/exact-object replay parity. Exact history must retain token envelope versus decrypted/validated representation, principal origin, binding rule and namespace; backwards seek must rebuild state deterministically and clear stale grants/results.

Provide a visible decision strip: credential → identity → requested action → matching grant → admission when relevant → result. Show why a step is skipped. Error cards name failing stage, caller identity, actual status and next meaningful action; do not map all 403s to RBAC.

Navigation, source/profile expanders and scenario switches need keyboard focus return, readable 390px layout, no token overflow, accessible branch labels and no color-only success signal. Keep five or fewer actors horizontally; break browser/login and API authorization into linked phases without losing artifacts.

Source panel pins release/profile/feature maturity, RFC section or Kubernetes section, retrieval date, implementation-specific cache policy and limits. Mark symbolic fixtures as symbolic; cryptographic validity requires separately computed test vectors rather than decorative signatures.

Tests should prove state boundaries and failure behavior, not mirror prose. Test route registration, all declared scenario IDs, preservation of existing OIDC/JWT/JWE paths, policy reset, identity mapping, exact-request RBAC decisions, JWT/key/token rotation, representation custody, no post-rejection persistence, and actual mounted field-to-exact-history transitions.

Before claiming runnable Kubernetes conformance, validate config/manifests and critical status/feature behavior against pinned v1.37.1 executable or source. Native-browser evidence remains separate from DOM tests and from live Kubernetes interoperability. Report any source discrepancy instead of inventing a consensus.

sourceGateRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
sourceGateRequirements.text: Create a new versioned planning/evidence area, for example docs/next-expansion/ and docs/verification/next-expansion/ . Preserve predecessor reports without relabeling them. Before implementing each family, write and retain an independently authored scenario worksheet and source matrix; generate completion reports from that contract and actual results, not the product's own final-state builder. Derive the runtime inventory from this plan’s 81-core/4-optional manifest; distinguish named variants from picker choices and count the Files SMB shortcut only once. Discover actual test totals from the suite rather than inventing a target count.

sourceGateRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
sourceGateRequirements.text: Scenario row: stable ID, workspace/family, learning question, implementation/platform/version, feature/configuration prerequisites, selected protocol/security profile, normative versus deployment-specific status, actor and trust boundaries, starting holdings, source section IDs, positive/negative outcome predicates, replay focus fields, related journeys and evidence IDs. A platform support claim needs its own dated official support source; existence in a standard does not prove a shipped OS/server supports it.

sourceGateRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
sourceGateRequirements.text: Source row: primary document URL, exact section and revision/version, retrieval date, applicable errata/update relationship, supported claim and any unresolved ambiguity. Pin MCP revision, Kubernetes release/configuration and OS/client/server profile assumptions in the corresponding lesson. Mark a standards-only or uncertain profile explicitly; never convert uncertainty into an invented universal behavior. Retain small relevant snapshots/fixture inputs with hashes where appropriate and give regeneration instructions.

sourceGateRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
sourceGateRequirements.text: Message and operation ledger: sender/receiver, exact representation, protection/key/context lineage, carried versus locally computed fields, receiver-local decode/check and canonical event/milestone. Distinguish network transfer, local IPC, local computation and an exchange folded onto one physical card. PAM, LSASS and LSM processing must use their actual local subsystem boundaries; never invent network packets to connect local checks, and do not turn genuine local IPC between different owners into a self-operation. Merely listing a field in prose or payload cannot establish its ownership or replay.

sourceGateRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
sourceGateRequirements.text: Object/holding ledger: separate artifact, representation and holding IDs; creator, exact value/reference, logical owner/store, permitted readers, acquire/use/release/replace events, derived-from identity and retained authority state. A ciphertext receipt grants only the wire holding until the authored decrypt/check event. Visibility, decoding, trust and acceptance are distinct: a signed JWT payload is readable before signature/claim validation and must be displayed as untrusted, not falsely hidden as ciphertext. Decoding alone never installs a trusted identity. Grant readable or accepted state only at the appropriate authored event for that representation; do not confuse the two grants. A failed check does not erase prior credential disclosure, credentials already cached, or the evidence that a message was received.

sourceGateRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
sourceGateRequirements.text: Outcome ledger: independently state server acceptance, client knowledge, session creation, authorization decision, protected-result receipt and result verification. For denials, say who knows what and when. A JWT signature, PAM authentication result, UAC/sudo authorization step, Kubernetes role match or NFS credential mapping must not automatically imply every later access decision.

sourceGateRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
sourceGateRequirements.text: Replay invariants: full journey, connection, field and exact-object replay must reconstruct the same complete canonical prefix at the same cursor. At least one meaningful local operation and one protected receipt/acceptance boundary per family need actual mounted replay checks. Verify exact value and representation, not merely a label or number of trace rows. Check reset, seek backward, replay exit and scenario/context change for stale secrets, holdings or selected objects.

sourceGateRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
sourceGateRequirements.text: Evidence identity: record exact source/manifest/worksheet hashes, runner hash, argv, exit status, runtime/browser/dependency versions, standalone hash/bytes, before/after identity, raw logs, screenshot hashes and findings. Keep failed/superseded runs with their status. Missing tools or incomplete scope produce an explicit unverified/partial result, never synthetic success. Reuse unchanged historical evidence only under its own identity and clearly bounded claim.

sourceGateRequirements.heading: Source, manifest and evidence contract
sourceGateRequirements.text: For numeric cryptographic claims, extend the isolated tools/verification/expansion-crypto/ verifier or a similarly isolated next-phase QA package. Pin dependencies and runtime, retain official vectors or independently generated deterministic fixtures and their provenance, and compare with an oracle independent of the application builder. Negative cases need documented mutated input and expected rejection, including wrong context/recipient/key where the profile requires it. Printing a fixture, recomputing an expected value with the same helper or passing a UI assertion is not numerical verification. Keep SYM(...) / HANDLE(...) material explicit whenever the lesson does not model real encoded bytes. No QA package becomes a runtime app dependency, no CDN/import/browser download is added to the application, and a numeric pass never becomes a live-platform interoperability claim.
